content: Digital diabetes prevention programs, including telehealth services and smartphone-based platforms, have demonstrated significant potential in improving health outcomes for individuals at risk of developing diabetes. These technology-driven interventions can increase accessibility to care and deliver personalized feedback, even for individuals residing in remote or underserved areas. Furthermore, such programs are capable of offering tailored guidance on physical activity and dietary management, addressing the specific needs of each individual. This personalized approach supports the adoption and maintenance of long-term lifestyle changes, which are critical for effective diabetes prevention.
